doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Invited to the White House and choosing her outfit
summary: The crowning point of her career was playing for President Clinton after Thelonious Monk suggested her; she wore a silver coat, baseball hat and rhinestone shoes.

blocks.x: I’d like to know what you think was the crowning point in your career? What was the most thrill for you as far as reaching a certain peak in your career?
Being invited to play before the President of the United States.
You’ll have to tell us about that.

Thelonious Monk had heard me in Switzerland. So, he asked me would I like to play at the White House. I said “Sure.” He said, “Well, I’ll let you know when I get back to America.” So, when I got back to America, he say, “It’s official.” But I noticed in the paper, they didn’t announce me. So, I learned later on the reason why. They say, the rest of them wouldn’t show up. So, I kept it under my hat . . .
Clinton. I played the Newport Jazz Festival.
Did you have a special dress you bought?
What did you pick out to wear?
I had a silver coat and a Chanel copy baseball hat.
A silver raincoat and what kind of a hat?
And a bugle beaded jet top and a black sequined skirt.
